passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Eusebius preserves a letter of Cornelius of Rome describing Novatian's ordination irregularity: three simple and rustic bishops from Italy were brought to Rome and compelled to lay hands on Novatian by a counterfeit and vain laying on of hands; Novatian seized the bishopric by craft and treachery. Cornelius also lists the Roman clergy: forty-six presbyters, seven deacons, seven subdeacons, forty-two acolytes, and fifty-two exorcists, readers, and doorkeepers. More than fifteen hundred widows and distressed persons are supported by the Lord's grace and kindness.

subject_entity.notes: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia c. 230–268; close ally of Origen and then of Cyprian in the rebaptism controversy; wrote a letter (Ep. 75 in Cyprian's collection) strongly supporting Cyprian's position that heretical baptism is invalid; attended the Synod of Antioch against Paul of Samosata but died en route c. 268.

object_entity.notes: Council held September 1, 256 under Cyprian's presidency with 87 North African bishops present; each bishop individually declared heretical baptism invalid and mandated rebaptism of converts from heretical groups; the fullest surviving example of North African collegial episcopal practice; opposed by Pope Stephen I of Rome.

context_place.notes: Major North African city; center of Latin Christianity from Tertullian through Cyprian and Augustine; seat of important regional councils.

evidence.notes: Eusebius HE 6.43 includes Firmilian's letter about the rebaptism controversy and councils.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: The episcopate is one, each part of which is held by each one for the whole. The Church also is one, which is spread abroad far and wide into a multitude by an increase of fruitfulness. As the sun has many rays but one light, and a tree has many branches but one strength, and as many streams flow from one spring — so also the Church, bathed in the light of the Lord, extends her rays over the whole world, yet it is one light that is diffused everywhere.
passage.notes: Episcopate held in solidum; Church unity through episcopal collegiality; sun/tree/stream metaphors
